findings.title: Budget spent total no longer filtered by month
findings.description: The new LEFT JOIN only matches `e.user_id = b.user_id AND e.category = b.category`; it never constrains expenses to the requested `month`/`spent_on` range the way the old `monthly_summary(db, user_id, month)` call did. As a result `spent` (and therefore `remaining` and `over_budget`) now aggregates ALL historical expenses in that category across every month, not just the target month. This is a behavior change (contrary to the PR description) that will silently report wildly inflated spend and incorrect over-budget flags for any user with expenses in prior months.

findings.title: CREATE INDEX statement lacks IF NOT EXISTS
findings.description: SCHEMA is run via `executescript` every time a Database object is constructed (i.e., on every app/process start against an existing database file). All other schema objects appear to be idempotent (implied by repeated execution working today), but `CREATE INDEX idx_expenses_user_category ON expenses (...)` has no `IF NOT EXISTS` guard. On any restart against a database that has already run this schema once, the statement will raise `sqlite3.OperationalError: index idx_expenses_user_category already exists`, crashing initialization for every existing deployment.

findings.title: synchronous=OFF risks database corruption
findings.description: Setting `PRAGMA synchronous = OFF` disables fsync calls at critical points; if the OS or application crashes (not just a power loss) between writes, SQLite makes no guarantee the database file won't become corrupted, not just lose recent transactions. For a financial ledger this is a serious durability/integrity regression. If faster writes are needed, `PRAGMA synchronous = NORMAL` combined with WAL mode is the safer standard trade-off; plain OFF is generally not recommended for any data users care about.

findings.title: No test coverage for month-scoping regression
findings.description: The PR changes the SQL powering `budget_status` but includes no new/updated tests verifying that spend is still scoped to the requested month (e.g., a budget with expenses in both the target month and an adjacent month). Such a test would have caught the missing month filter in the LEFT JOIN before merge.
